speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that your psychiatric symptoms have improved significantly on risperidone. To help me understand the movement disorder, can you describe exactly what the abnormal movements look like and when they occur? For instance, are they involuntary jerking movements, stiffness, or a feeling of restlessness that makes you unable to sit still?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—restlessness, pacing, and fidgeting—are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of risperidone. Do you feel an internal sense of anxiety or unease that drives this need to move, and have you noticed these movements worsening since your last dose?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the absence of substance use helps rule out other causes. Since this appears to be acute akathisia induced by risperidone, have you experienced any muscle stiffness, tremors, or facial grimacing along with this restlessness?
